info.title: knime-orchestador API
info.description: The JSON API the admin frontend consumes.

get.summary:
Handle `GET /audit/events?limit=`: the most recent audit events, newest
first, capped at [`MAX_LIMIT`] regardless of what the caller asks for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 50, capped at 200).

403.description: Authenticated but not the admin role

get.summary: `GET /auth/captcha`: which key to render the captcha with, if any.

200.description: The Turnstile site key, if a captcha is used

post.summary: Handle `POST /auth/login`.
post.description:
`200` with the admin id and fresh session/CSRF cookies on success; `401`
for invalid credentials (identical for a wrong password and a nonexistent
account); `429` with `Retry-After` when the IP or account has hit the
app-level rate limit, or when the account/IP is locked out (see
[`LoginError::TooManyAttempts`] — a distinct mechanism from the rate limit:
lockout counts *failures*, the rate limit counts *every* attempt); `503`
when the directory (LDAP / AD) does not answer; `500` on an internal
failure. Every successful login issues a brand-new session —
there is no "reuse the prior session" path — which is what satisfies
session rotation on login.

200.description: Signed in; sets session and csrf cookies

401.description: Invalid credentials (wrong password or unknown account)

422.description: Malformed request (per-field validation)

429.description: Rate-limited or locked out; carries Retry-After

503.description: The directory (LDAP / AD) is not responding

post.summary:
Handle `POST /auth/logout`: revoke the session server-side, record the
event to the audit trail, and clear both cookies. Requires (via
[`require_session`]) a valid session and a matching CSRF header — logout
is a mutation like any other.

204.description: Logged out; clears the session and csrf cookies

get.summary:
Handle `GET /auth/me`: report the authenticated admin's identity and
profile fields, so the frontend can display them without a separate round
trip. Any authenticated role may call this — it is not itself role-gated
(see [`require_role`](crate::http::rbac::require_role) for endpoints that are).

200.description: The authenticated admin's identity and profile

get.summary:
`GET /auth/me/identities`: the external identities linked to the signed-in
admin.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /auth/me/identities/{provider}/{subject}`: unlink one of the
signed-in admin's identities. `404` when they have no such link.

put.summary: Handle `PUT /auth/me/locale`: remember the admin's interface language.

422.description: Not a supported language

get.summary:
`GET /auth/oauth/providers`: list the enabled provider ids. Public — the
login page calls it before any session exists.

post.summary: Handle `POST /auth/password-reset/check`.

200.description: Whether the link works, and the password policy

post.summary: Handle `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm`.
post.description:
`204` once the password is changed (every session of the account ends, so
the person signs in again); `410` when the link no longer works; `422` with
the unmet rules when the password is too weak (the link keeps working).

204.description: Password changed; every session of the account ended

410.description: The link is invalid, used or expired

422.description: The password does not meet the policy

post.summary: Handle `POST /auth/password-reset/request`.

202.description: If the account exists, a link is on its way

422.description: Malformed email

503.description: Outgoing mail is not configured

get.summary:
Liveness probe: `200 OK` whenever the process is running. No dependency is
checked, so a slow or briefly-unreachable database never turns into a restart.

`GET /install/ca.crt`: the installation's CA, which `join.sh` checks
against `--ca-sha256` before it sends the token anywhere.

200.description: The CA, PEM; its SHA-256 (of its DER) in X-Content-SHA256

503.description: The installation has no CA

the machine's certificate.

409.description: Another machine has that name, or the token is another node's

422.description: A bad name or signing request; the token is not used

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

503.description: The installation has no CA

get.summary:
`GET /install/join.sh`: the script the join command runs once its
SHA-256 is checked.

503.description: This API serves no installation files

401.description: No join token, or one unknown, used, expired or of another role

404.description: No such file for that role

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

503.description: This API serves no installation files

get.summary:
`GET /install/{role}/pool.env`: a lake pool node's layout (0066 step

get.summary:
`GET /install/{role}/root-keys.env`: RustFS's root keys of the lake a

200.description: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY and RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, an environment file

401.description: No join token, or one unknown, used, expired or of another role

404.description: No root keys for that role

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

503.description: This API serves no installation files

applied.description: Alerts kept, changed or removed, the heartbeat's included.

unknown.description: Alerts left out: of a machine unknown or retired, or naming none.

site_key.description: Turnstile's public key; `null`: no captcha is asked.

id.description: Its id, the key of its texts in the web.

kind.description: How the web draws it: `bar`, `line`, `scatter` or `table`.

needs.description:
The field roles it needs from a dataset ([`crate::mapping::FieldRole`]
by name).

ChartRows.description: One chart's rows for a cut.

cut.description: The cut shown; none if the dataset has no evaluated cut.

rows.description: One object per row, its columns as the chart's query names them.

ChartsOut.description: A dataset's dashboard: its charts and the cuts they can show.

CheckBody.description: A rules file to check, of `dataset`.

draft.description:
The draft it is typed on: checked with that draft's global rules
(decision 0045); `main`'s otherwise.

file.description:
The file's name, to say which rules are not in their field's file
(decision 0044).

CheckOut.description: What a rules file says, as typed.

fields.description:
The fields of the dataset's mapping, for completion (only when
checked through `POST /quality/rules/check`).

column.description: The column, as the source names it.

type.description:
Its type in the source (`VARCHAR`, `INTEGER`, `DATE`…): the
field's type in silver follows from it.

Confirm.description: The name of what is deleted, typed again.

ConsoleAsk.description: A statement to run: one query over the lake's tables (`lake.<ns>.<table>`).

ConsoleOut.description: A statement as its asker sees it: `queued`, `running`, `done` or `failed`.

masked.description: Whether the values are masked: always on a read, never on a reveal.

revealable.description:
Whether a reveal would show values: the result has rows or an
engine message and the caller holds the permission that shows them.

ConsoleResult.description:
What a `query` job read: its columns and rows as text (`null` where
empty), whether there were more, or the engine's message if it failed.

error.description: The engine's message; it may quote a value.

activation_sent.description:
`false` when the account was created but the email could not be sent
(send it again from the list).

CutOut.description: A dataset's cut, as the screen shows it.

failed_at.description:
Failed: at `extract` or `evaluate`, and what its job said (the
worker's words, which name no value).

manifest.description: Its evaluation's manifest in the warehouse bucket, once evaluated.

records.description: The records its evaluation read, once evaluated.

run.description: 1, and one more each time it was replaced.

scheduled.description: Fired by a schedule; else asked by a person (_Run now_).

DatasetFrom.description:
A source's table: the source by name, its schema if the mapping names
one, and the table.

DatasetOut.description:
A dataset of the catalog's `main`, and where its mapping reads it
(decision 0043, point 1): nothing of it if the mapping does not read.

bronze.description: Its table in the lake's `<name>_bronze` namespace.

fields.description: Each field of the mapping and the column it reads.

oneOf.description:
The source's table an extraction reads; none for a dataset loaded
into the lake by hand.

last_cut.description:
Its latest cut's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); none before its first run
(decision 0049: _no cuts yet_).

DeployBody.description: A column's file to deploy, and the file as the person opened it.

expected.description: `main`'s file when it was opened; `null` if it had none.

DoltHoldOut.description: Whether Dolt is free, and if so the catalog held.

free.description:
No operation of the catalog in flight in the API and no statement
running in Dolt: the catalog is held until released or 5 minutes.
Otherwise nothing is held: ask again later.

in_flight.description: The catalog's operations in flight in the API now.

running.description:
The other connections running a statement in Dolt; `null` if it was
not asked or did not answer.

released.description: `false` when there was none in force (it had expired by itself).

parent.description: The commit it follows (the first follows `main`'s).

DraftHistory.description: A draft's commits, newest first, and the commit of `main` it left from.

DraftInfo.description: A draft as the catalog lists it.

DraftOut.description:
A draft to review: its mapping and its rules files, each with the codes
of its lint errors.

mapping_reads.description: Whether the mapping reads; if not, nothing else is checked.

DriverFieldOut.description: One field of a driver's form; a `secret` one is never sent back.

DriverOut.description: A driver of the catalog, for its form.

EngineOut.description: The engine that reads a driver's sources.

ErrorResponse.description: The JSON body every error response carries.

fields.description: Per-field validation messages, present only on a `422` response.

message.description: A human-readable, client-safe message. Never contains internal detail.

trace_id.description:
A correlation id, also logged server-side, so a client-reported error
can be matched to its log line.

EventOut.description: One audit event, as returned to the admin panel.

action.description: The IAM action it was done under, for an event on a module's resource.

admin_id.description: The resolved admin id, when the event maps to a known account.

email_attempted.description:
The email submitted, for login events (kept even when it matched no
account).

fields_shown.description:
For a view of values, the names of the columns or fields it showed,
in order (a console column that is not a plain identifier by its
position, `#2`). Never a value.

ip.description: The client IP the request came from.

job_id.description:
The job, for credentials issued to one (the machine is in
`service_account`), and for a view of values its view's job.

occurred_at_epoch.description: When the event happened, as Unix epoch seconds.

purpose.description:
For a view of values, why it was revealed: a purpose's key
(`quality_review`, `rule_writing`, `remediation`, `client_request`,
`audit`, `other`, or one no longer offered). Absent before decision
0069 and for every other event.

reference.description:
For a view of values, the ticket or case number it was revealed
under, if given.

resource.description: The resource it was done on (`source/core`).

rows_shown.description: For a view of values, how many rows it showed.

service_account.description: The service account it came with, or the machine.

ExtendsOut.description: A rule's `extends`: the named rule, and the line where it is cited.

FailGroup.description:
Failures of one shape (each digit `9`, each letter `A`): how many, and
a few of them.

FieldColumn.description: A field of a mapping and the column it reads.

FieldValue.description: A field's value in a record read; `null` where empty.

FieldsBody.description: A table's columns to read as fields.

columns.description: Every column of the table; those a field reads already are left.

oneOf.description:
The table, when no dataset reads it: the dataset is started
reading it.

FieldsOut.description: `main`'s commit with the fields, and the fields.

FileChange.description: A file before and after; `null` where it was not.

file.description: A rules file's name, or `mapping` for the dataset's mapping.

FindingOut.description: A lint finding: its `QR` code, how serious, where and what it says.

GrafanaAlertIn.description: One alert, as Grafana's webhook sends it; its other fields are ignored.

fingerprint.description: Letters and digits, up to 64: Grafana's id of the alert.

values.description: Each query's number (`A`, `C`); anything else is not kept.

GrafanaDeliveryIn.description: Grafana's webhook body; only `alerts` is read.

IdentitiesOut.description: The identities linked to the signed-in admin.

IdentityOut.description: One external identity linked to the signed-in admin.

email.description: The email the provider reported, if any.

linked_at.description: When it was linked, in Unix epoch seconds.

subject.description: The provider's subject id — what unlinking names.

InUse.description: The datasets whose mapping on the catalog's `main` reads the source.

JoinCommandOut.description: The command Settings shows to add the machine, with every hash in it.

ca_sha256.description: The CA's SHA-256 (of its DER), which the script checks: `--ca-sha256`.

command.description: The command to run on the new server, as root; it holds the token.

script_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of `join.sh`, which the command checks before running it.

csr.description:
The PKCS#10 signing request of its EC P-256 key, PEM. Only its key
is used: subject, names and lifetime are the CA's.

name.description:
The machine's name, its certificate's `CN`: lowercase letters,
digits and hyphens.

token.description: The join token from Settings → Execution (`qdj_…`).

not_after.description:
When it ends, in Unix epoch seconds: a day, or a year for a role
that takes its certificate only at a restart (Trino's coordinator).

state.description: `pending`: it gets no work until a person approves it.

JoinTokenIn.description: What a join token is for.

drives.description:
The mounted paths of a lake replica's or a pool node's drives, for its command to
carry a `--drive` for each: absolute, of letters, digits, `.`, `_`,
`-` and `/`, each once, at most 16. Refused for a role that takes
none. Left out or empty, the command has no `--drive` and the person
adds them by hand.

node.description:
For the role `lake` alone, required: the node of the pool the token
is for, one of the pool's (`PUT /lake/pools/{name}`). Only a machine
of that name joins with it, and the command names it (`--name`).

pool.description: Its pool: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

role.description: The role of the machine that joins with it.

JoinTokenOut.description: A join token: shown here once, never again.

expires_at.description: When it stops working (an hour), in Unix epoch seconds.

oneOf.description:
The command that installs the machine, with its hashes; absent for
a role nothing installs yet, or without an HTTPS public address.

node.description: The lake pool's node it is for.

LabelledLineOut.description: One labelled line of a machine: a filesystem by its watched path's name.

values.description: A value for each point, `null` where there is none.

LakeAdminKeysIn.description: The keys shown on the lake's server, pasted.

LakeAdminKeysOut.description: What is kept of a lake's admin keys: never the secret.

access_key.description: The access key, as `join.sh` showed it.

set_at.description: When they were pasted last, in Unix epoch seconds.

drives.description: The drives of each node, 1 to 16.

nodes.description:
The nodes' names, in order: 4 to 16, each a host's name its peers
resolve (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at either end).

ListingReason.description:
Why a listing's last attempt failed, from the worker's message (which
names the stage, never a value of the source).

ListingView.description: A source's last listing, and whether a newer one is coming.

attempt.description: While retrying: the attempt coming or running, of `max_attempts`.

oneOf.description: While retrying or failed: why the last attempt failed.

locale.description: `es`, `en`, or `null` to follow the browser again.

LoginBody.description: The JSON body of a login request.

captcha.description: The Turnstile token, when the API asked for it (`captcha_required`).

LoginOk.description: The success body: the authenticated administrator's id.

available.description:
`false` when Mimir did not answer in time, or is not read here: no
machine is listed, and the charts say "metrics not available".

end.description: The last point, in Unix epoch seconds.

machines.description: By name; only machines not retired that Mimir has series of.

start.description: The first point, in Unix epoch seconds.

cert_not_after.description: When that certificate ends, in Unix epoch seconds.

cert_serial.description: The serial of the certificate in use (lowercase hex).

cert_serial_next.description:
A renewed certificate it has not presented yet: accepted too, and the
one in use once presented.

created_at.description: In Unix epoch seconds, as the other times.

MachineSeriesOut.description: One machine's series; a list is empty when Mimir has none of it.

last_sample.description: Its last host sample within the range, in Unix epoch seconds.

MachinesOut.description: The machines, and whether new ones can join.

can_join.description: `false` while the installation has no CA: no token can be issued.

MainChange.description:
A change on `main` to one file: the commit that made it, and the file
before and after.

MainLakeStateOut.description: The main lake, as the application sees it now.

detail.description: With `unreachable`: what happened, as the connection said it.

drives_online.description: With `answered`: its drives online and offline.

MapBody.description: Which table to map, and the dataset it becomes.

dataset.description: The dataset's name: `a-z`, `0-9`, `_`, starting with a letter.

sample.description: Rows to profile; 10,000 when left out.

table.description: `table` or `schema.table`, as the source names it.

MapOut.description: The map job queued, and the dataset it makes.

MapProgress.description: How far a map went: its job, then the dataset's first cut.

oneOf.description: Once mapped, the dataset's latest cut.

error.description: What the job said when it failed (the worker's words, no value).

MeOut.description:
The body `GET /auth/me` returns: enough for the frontend to know who is
logged in and which role's guards to apply, plus profile fields for the UI.

avatar.description:
The profile picture's version (when it changed, Unix seconds), to load
it from `/auth/me/avatar?v=…`; `null` without one.

commit.description: The commit the server was built from, when it is a release build.

display_name.description: An optional display name for the profile UI.

locale.description:
The interface language the admin chose (`es` / `en`); `null` follows
the browser.

version.description: The server's version (the release tag), shown in the UI for debugging.

NewDraftBody.description: A rules file of `main`, edited: the draft it starts.

PasswordPolicyOut.description: The password rules a new password must meet.

PoolNodeOut.description: A pool's node, and the machine that joined as it.

machine_id.description: The machine's id, for Settings → Execution.

state.description:
The machine's state once it joined (`pending`, `approved` or
`draining`); absent until it does.

ProvidersOut.description: The configured OAuth providers, for the login UI to render a button per one.

providers.description:
The enabled provider ids (e.g. `["google"]`), sorted. Empty when OAuth
is configured but has no providers; the whole route is absent (`404`)
when OAuth is disabled entirely — the UI treats both as "no providers".

RecordsAsk.description:
What is asked of a source's table: page `page` (from 0) of [`PAGE`]
records, in `order` if given (descending if `descending`: the last ones
first), else as the engine gives them.

table.description: `schema.table`, as the source's listing names it.

RecordsOut.description: A page as its asker sees it: `queued`, `running`, `done` or `failed`.

masked.description: Whether the values are masked: always on a read, never on a reveal.

revealable.description:
Whether a reveal would show values: the page has records and the
caller holds the permission that shows them whole.

RecordsPage.description:
A page of a source table's records, as the job reports it: the columns
in the table's order, each record's values as text (`None` where empty),
and whether there are more after it.

Refusal.description:
One reason a source is refused: a code the UI's texts translate, and the
field it is about.

Refusals.description: Every reason a source is refused.

RenewIn.description: A machine asks for a new certificate.

csr.description:
The PKCS#10 signing request of a new EC P-256 key, PEM. Only its key
is used: subject, names and lifetime are the CA's.

certificate.description: Its certificate, PEM: the same `O=qd, OU=<role>, CN=<name>`.

not_after.description:
When it ends, in Unix epoch seconds: a day, or a year for Trino's
coordinator.

serial.description:
The new certificate's serial, lowercase hex. Until the machine first
presents it, the one it renewed with is accepted too.

ReplicaStateOut.description: The replica, as the application sees it now.

detail.description: With `unreachable`: what happened, as the connection said it.

drives_online.description: With `answered`: its drives online and offline.

machine.description: The replica's machine, when there is one.

machines.description: With `several_machines`: the approved or draining ones.

pending.description: With `no_machine`: one that joined and waits to be approved.

ReplicationOut.description: The replication, as Settings → Lake shows it.

noncurrent_days.description: After how many days the main lake's noncurrent versions expire.

readiness.description:
`ready`, `no_address` (no main lake), `no_replica` (none, or
several, approved) or `no_keys`.

retention_days.description: The replica's default retention (`COMPLIANCE`), in days.

source.description:
With `ready`: the main lake and the replica's node; `proxy` is no
longer said (the lake's adapter works it out) and stays null.

token.description: The token from the link (the part after `#`).

valid.description: `false` for a link that is unknown, used, replaced or expired.

ResetConfirmBody.description: Set a new password with a reset link.

token.description: The token from the link (the part after `#`).

captcha.description: The Turnstile token (required when the API uses a captcha).

ResetRequestOut.description: The answer to a reset request, the same for every email.

expires_in_minutes.description: How long the emailed link works, in minutes.

RevealIn.description:
Why values are revealed: a purpose's key and, for a ticket or case, a
reference (required with `other`).

purpose.description: A key of the fixed list; another is refused with 422 `purpose`.

reference.description:
At most 32 ASCII characters (`INC-2041`): letters, digits and
`-_/#.`, the first a letter or digit, at least one letter.

RuleTested.description: One rule's counts on the cut and its read of records.

groups.description: Its failures grouped by the shape of what it read, largest first.

duckdb.description: Its SQL on DuckDB, unless it reads a reference not resolved here.

oneOf.description:
The named rule it extends and the line that says so: this rule,
as read, is what it does (decision 0045).

kind.description: Of one field, or across fields; in words.

pattern.description: Its pattern as the YAML writes it (`required`, `format`, …).

reads.description:
The dataset's fields it reads, each once; a derived field's are
those it is computed from (decision 0043, point 2).

errors.description: The codes of its lint errors: none to approve.

commit.description: The `main` commit they were read at.

mapping_reads.description: Whether the dataset's mapping reads; if not, no rule is read.

RunBody.description: What to do when today's cut is already there.

rerun.description:
`block` (the default) or `replace`: a cut still extracting or
evaluating is never replaced.

ScheduleBody.description: A schedule as a person writes it.

cron.description:
Five fields: minute hour day month weekday (`0 6 * * 1-5`); left
out with a trigger.

dataset.description: A cut's and a `map`'s; none for a `maintain` of the whole warehouse.

enabled.description: `true` when left out; a schedule with cuts is disabled, not deleted.

fires.description: `cut` (extraction, then evaluation) or `job` (one that needs no cut).

timezone.description: IANA; the platform's time zone when left out (UTC if it has none).

trigger.description:
In the style of the Windows Task Scheduler: a start, how often
(`once`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`), and repetition, a random
delay and expiry. When given, the schedule fires by it, not by `cron`.

ScheduleOut.description: A schedule, with what the scheduler keeps of it.

cron.description: Empty when it fires by its trigger.

ScheduleRefusal.description: Why a schedule is refused: a code the UI's texts translate.

Sla.description: One queue's SLA, or a dimension's default.

group.description:
One of its values (`""` is the empty value's group); none for the
dimension's default.

SlaRefusal.description: Why SLAs are refused: a code the UI's texts translate.

SlasBody.description: A dataset's SLAs, every one: those left out go back to their default.

SlasOut.description: A dataset's SLAs and what a form needs to set them.

default_days.description: A queue's days when neither its group nor its dimension has an SLA.

dimensions.description:
The fields holding the `dimension` role in its mapping on `main`;
none without a catalog or a mapping that reads.

slas.description: By dimension, its default first, then its groups.

SourceBody.description: A source as the form sends it: secrets left out keep their value.

SourceColumn.description: A column as the source's catalog declares it.

data_type.description:
As the engine reads the source's type: DuckDB's (`INTEGER`,
`DECIMAL(14,2)`).

SourceTable.description: One table of a source, as a map job names it (`schema.table`).

SourceView.description: A source as people see it: its secrets only by name.

previous.description: Whether a previous version is kept.

secrets.description: The secret fields that are set.

secrets_set_at.description: When the current secrets were written (RFC 3339).

TableBody.description: A table no dataset reads: a source's, or the lake's (no source).

table.description: `schema.table` of a source; the table's name in the lake.

TestBody.description:
A rules file as typed, to test on `dataset`'s latest cut; `rule` only
that rule.

columns.description:
Fields of the dataset to show in the records read, besides the key
and those a rule reads; any of the mapping's, all of them if asked.

TestOut.description:
A test as its asker sees it: `queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed` or
`expired`.

masked.description: Whether the values are masked: always on a read, never on a reveal.

revealable.description:
Whether a reveal would show values: the report has records and the
caller holds the permission that shows them whole.

state.description:
`queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed`, or `expired`: done, its report
no longer kept (a day), so none is answered; test again.

TestReport.description: What a `test_rule` job found, as its worker reports it.

records.description: The records of the cut the test read.

TestStarted.description: The test queued: its job and the cut it reads.

TestedRecord.description:
A record a rule was run on: `fails`, `passes` or `skips` (does not
apply), with its key's values first, then those of the fields the rule
reads.

TidyBody.description: A rules file, to tidy or tidied.

UpdateUserIn.description: An account's new name and role.

created_at.description: When it was created, in Unix epoch seconds.

role.description: `admin` or `user` (or another role from the directory).

status.description:
`active` (has a password), `pending` (waiting for its activation) or
`directory` (signs in with LDAP / AD).

UsersOut.description: The accounts, plus what the creation form needs.

mail_configured.description: Whether outgoing mail is configured (creating an account needs it).

roles.description: The roles a new account can get.

ViewPurpose.description:
Why values were revealed: one of a fixed list (decision 0069, point 6).
The keys are stable: one is never renamed, and the list only grows.

WarehouseReplicationOut.description: One warehouse, as the last run left it.

checked_at.description: When it was configured or tried last, in Unix epoch seconds.

configured_at.description: When it was first configured, in Unix epoch seconds.

detail.description: With `failed`: what happened, in a few words.

state.description:
`configured`, `made` (made on the main lake, its replication
waiting for the replica or its keys), `no_warehouse` (not on the
main lake yet), `no_keys` or `failed`.

step.description:
With `failed`: the step (`warehouse_bucket` and `warehouse_tables`,
making the warehouse on the main lake; `source_bucket`, `replica_bucket`,
`replica_retention`, `source_versioning`, `source_lifecycle`,
`remote_target`, `rule`).
